# PHB Frontend – Copilot Guide

- Stack: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite; styling via Tailwind plus MUI/Fluent components; routing with React Router v6; state via React Contexts (no Redux). Build outputs to `dist/` for Netlify.
- Common commands (npm-first): `npm run dev`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run preview`, `npm run deploy` (Netlify). Bun equivalents exist (`bun run ...`) but npm is the default in practice.
- Environment: API roots set in Vite vars; `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is normalized to localhost for cookie safety in [src/utils/config.ts](src/utils/config.ts). Use `createApiUrl()` from the same file to avoid double slashes; APIs also expose `API_URL`, `AUTH_API_URL`, `HEALTH_API_URL`, `ORGANIZATION_API_URL` for service-specific calls.
- Authentication (patients/general): `AuthProvider` in [src/features/auth/authContext.tsx](src/features/auth/authContext.tsx) uses httpOnly cookies with `credentials: 'include'`; no Authorization header needed. It auto-refreshes tokens every ~25 minutes, handles OTP, CAPTCHA, onboarding flags, and caches hospital lookups; respect its helpers instead of duplicating fetch logic.
- Authentication (professionals): `ProfessionalAuthProvider` in [src/features/professional/professionalAuthContext.tsx](src/features/professional/professionalAuthContext.tsx) derives from the main user and augments from the registry API (`/api/registry/my-info/`). State is stored in localStorage (`phb_professional_auth_state`, `phb_view_preference`); planned migration to cookies—avoid adding new localStorage keys.
- Authentication (organizations): `OrganizationAuthProvider` in [src/features/organization/organizationAuthContext.tsx](src/features/organization/organizationAuthContext.tsx) is cookie-based, with OTP/2FA flows and aggressive refresh on timers, tab focus, and user activity. It keeps only non-sensitive flags in sessionStorage; do not persist org user data elsewhere.
- Routing: [src/App.tsx](src/App.tsx) wires the entire site—public health content, patient account, professional, and organization areas. Layout wrappers live in `src/layouts`; guards include Protected routes for patients, professional/organization route guards, and `HospitalStatusGuard` for appointment flows. When adding routes, nest under the correct layout and provider.
- Feature organization: reusable UI in `src/components`; domain logic in `src/features` (health, auth, search, etc.); page-level views in `src/pages`; shared helpers in `src/utils` and `src/lib`; styles in `src/styles` plus Tailwind in `src/index.css`.
- Health/appointment flows: booking, viewing, confirmation, detail views under `src/features/health` with API helpers in `src/services` (e.g., appointment/payment/medical records). Keep `credentials: 'include'` on fetch/axios to preserve cookies.
- Advanced search system: assembled in [src/features/search/AdvancedSearchPage.tsx](src/features/search/AdvancedSearchPage.tsx) with supporting components (body map, symptom checker, medical dictionary). Refer to [docs/search/README.md](docs/search/README.md) before changing search flows or dictionaries.
- Onboarding/auth docs: see [docs/authentication-flow.md](docs/authentication-flow.md) and [docs/onboarding-flow.md](docs/onboarding-flow.md) for expected API shapes and UI steps; align new auth screens with these contracts.
- API tokens and storage conventions: all auth/medical tokens live in httpOnly cookies or in-memory; do not add localStorage/sessionStorage token writes. Allowed localStorage keys are limited to `phb_view_preference`, `cookie-consent`, and optional wellness tool state. Session storage flags `phb_logout_flag` (patients) and `org_logout_flag` (orgs) distinguish intentional logout.
- Styling: Tailwind is primary; legacy MUI/Fluent components exist—match the surrounding style rather than mixing systems arbitrarily. Prefer utility classes and `tailwind-merge` for overrides.
- Forms and validation: most auth/health forms expect JSON payloads and server-side errors surfaced from fetch responses; reuse existing request helpers instead of bare `fetch` to keep consistent error handling and throttling.
- Deployment: Netlify config lives in `netlify.toml`; `deploy` script assumes Netlify CLI auth. Vercel config exists but Netlify is primary.
- Licensing: project is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial); keep attribution notices intact.
